This game started the whole "ghost hunting" trend but it's become amazingly obvious that the devs had no vision or ideas past the initial concept. Recent updates have actually made the game worse in many ways by introducing bugs that hinder normal play (ghosts don't interact with evidence or don't behave as the journal says they should, etc) and stated features have been pushed back time and time and time again for years all while news posts from the devs are trying to sell merch to a playerbase that is begging for changes to be rolled back.

The final straw for me was this character model update, something the devs have been "working on" for over a year now but came rolling out like the result of a weekend bender and a last-minute term paper. The models are laughably bad (looking down at your feet you can easily see that your shoes are on the wrong feet), the animations and rigging are janky and broken (notice in the screenshots all the characters are using the tier 2 flashlight, that's because the tier 3 flashlight causes your character to hold the item like their wrist is snapped), and the art director admitted that they rushed the update out in order to push an Alan Wake crossover event. Don't worry though, he assures us that most problems are "quick fixes" and that "once you get used to it, you might forget some of the jank."

The game has been in early access for 6 years and in that time it has stagnated and fallen behind other games in the genre that push forward and try to add ideas and mechanics to the basic gameplay loop. Sad to see the game that started the trend in such a state, but hey, at least they have a movie coming out. A movie about the spooky ghost game you play with your friends, a game that has no narrative thread or story or even any named characters (before the rushed hack job of a character model update anyway).

Just wait for their 1.0 release and see if anything got fixed or addressed before buying, or just avoid it completely and save yourself the time and trouble of putting more work in than the people being paid to make the game.

After nearly 6 years and hundreds of millions in revenue, one of the most enjoyable ghost hunting games (Phasmophobia) has been ruined by a single update. An update that no one asked for and no one wanted. I spent part of the day playing the new update on the PS5 with a few friends. We all quit within an hour after realizing how badly the update had damaged the game we've enjoyed for so many years.

No, we don't need to see a giant first person character's hand slowly, slowly, SLOWLY, turn on a UV light, EMF reader, or Spirit Box. We don't need to see that hand take up 25% of the screen. We don't need to see a character period because this isn't Cyberpunk. The amount of janky character animations are bad enough, but the truth is that adding the character at all has ruined the immersion of this game. That's not even including the horrendous character customization which is laughably bad and oddly restrictive to the character you choose. But hey, you can choose from 2-3 pairs of pants for thousands of in game dollars.

Tanglewood has also been completely reworked. There's no legacy or classic options for the original layout of the level so hopefully you like the Choo Choo Train. Sure, some might enjoy the new look of the tiny map, but again, I don't believe kinetic understands how such a simple and classic game can be ruined when creative choices destroy the core of it. That core that made the game so appealing to begin with and that design that players fell in love with. Even the death animation for our characters is new and also oddly unsatisfying and janky looking. Who greenlit these decisions?

All of this energy could have been saved for new ghosts, new maps, or a sequel. I am actually in shock by how badly Kinetic missed the mark here with the substance and execution of this "update." My only hope is that this update is rolled back and forgotten about...Until then, I won't return and definitely won't recommend this game to anyone.
